exam.why: External failures are discovered after the product or service reaches the customer, such as credits, returns and warranty claims.

exam.q: During a maturity assessment, a leader rates performance measurement as Managed (4), but no team can show a current KPI board. What score is most defensible?
opts: A lower score, because there is no visible evidence
4, because the leader knows the business best
5, because KPIs exist in the ERP
Skip the dimension until data is available
exam.why: Scores must be backed by evidence a visitor could see. Without it, the score should come down.

exam.q: On a gemba walk, what is the best first action when you arrive at the work area?
opts: Point out any 5S problems you notice
Ask the supervisor for the latest KPI report
Suggest solutions to the first problem you see
Observe the work for several minutes before asking questions
exam.why: Gemba walks start with observation so you see the real process before forming opinions or asking questions.

exam.q: A team building a SIPOC lists the process steps first. What should it typically do next?
opts: Detail every decision point in swim lanes
Calculate process cycle efficiency
List outputs and customers
Write standard work
exam.why: SIPOC is built from the middle out: process steps, then outputs and customers, then inputs and suppliers.

exam.q: A repair order takes 5 working days (40 working hours) from arrival to shipment, with 4 hours of hands-on work. What is the process cycle efficiency?
exam.why: Process cycle efficiency is value-added time divided by lead time: 4 / 40 = 10%.

exam.q: Nurses in a clinic spend part of each shift photocopying and filing forms. Which of the 8 wastes is the clearest fit?
opts: Overproduction
Transportation
Inventory
Non-utilized talent
exam.why: Highly skilled staff doing clerical work is non-utilized talent; their skills could be applied to patient care.

exam.q: Which is the best-written gap statement?
opts: Changeovers are too slow
Changeovers on Line 2 average 80 minutes against a 30-minute target, costing about 5 hours of capacity a week
We need SMED training
Line 2 has problems with its operators
exam.why: A good gap statement describes the current state, the desired state and the impact in measurable terms.

exam.q: A distribution centre measures pickers only on lines picked per hour. Picking errors start to rise. What is the best KPI fix?
opts: Pair the speed measure with a picking accuracy measure
Raise the lines-per-hour target
Stop measuring pickers altogether
Measure errors only once a quarter
exam.why: Pairing measures prevents gaming. Speed is balanced by accuracy so teams optimize the right behaviour.

exam.q: A machine has 400 minutes of planned time, 40 minutes of downtime, an ideal cycle time of 1 minute, 300 total parts and 285 good parts. What is its availability?
exam.why: Availability = run time / planned time = (400 - 40) / 400 = 90%.

exam.q: Using the same machine (360 minutes run time, 1-minute ideal cycle, 300 total parts, 285 good), which factor is the largest loss?
opts: Availability
Quality
All three are equal
Performance
exam.why: Performance = 300 / 360 = 83.3%, lower than availability (90%) and quality (95%), so speed loss is largest.

exam.q: A supervisor wants to discipline a team after one bad day of quality results, though the run chart shows that level has occurred several times with no pattern. What does this suggest?
opts: Common cause variation; reacting to it may make things worse
A special cause that needs investigation
The measurement system is broken
The target is set correctly
exam.why: Points within the normal range with no pattern are common cause variation. Improvement requires changing the process, not reacting to single points.

exam.q: A 5 Whys analysis on a late shipment stops at "the driver forgot to load one pallet." What should the team do?
opts: Accept it and retrain the driver
Switch to a fishbone diagram and start over
Close the issue because it was a one-time event
Keep asking why the process allowed a pallet to be missed
exam.why: Human error is rarely the root cause. Asking why the process allowed it leads to error-proofing, such as a load checklist or staging lane.

exam.q: A complex, high-impact scrap problem has unclear causes and several interacting factors. Which approach fits best?
opts: A single PDCA cycle over one shift
A 5S event in the area
A DMAIC project with a charter, measured baseline and verified root causes
A new KPI board
exam.why: DMAIC is designed for complex problems with unknown causes and high stakes, using data to verify causes before solutions.

exam.q: A RACI for a new procurement process lists four people as Consulted on every task and no front-line buyer as Responsible. What is the most important fix?
opts: Make the front-line buyers Responsible for tasks they perform and trim unnecessary Consulted roles
Add more Informed roles
Remove the Accountable role
Make everyone Accountable
exam.why: Too many Consulted roles slow decisions, and front-line staff should be Responsible for the work they do so improvements are designed with them.

exam.q: Using ADKAR, a team knows why a change is happening but sees no benefit for themselves and keeps arguing against it. Which element should a leader address first?
opts: Knowledge
Desire
Ability
Reinforcement
exam.why: Awareness is present but desire is missing. Addressing their concerns and involving them in design builds desire before training.

exam.q: A kaizen team cut changeover time in half, but first-piece rejects doubled. Which charter element would have flagged this early?
opts: The sponsor's name
A longer timeline
A larger team
A balancing measure for first-piece quality
exam.why: A balancing measure protects against improvements in one area that create problems in another.

exam.q: In a Tier 1 huddle, the team's board shows ten open issues, most overdue, with no owners. What is the best improvement to the huddle?
opts: Make the huddle longer
Remove the issues list from the board
Assign an owner and date to each issue or escalate it, and review overdue items daily
Hold the huddle weekly instead
exam.why: Effective huddles give every issue an owner and date or escalate it, and they check overdue items every day.

exam.q: A company wants to spread a successful loading standard from one yard to another that services different equipment. What is the best approach?
opts: Let the receiving crew see the original, then adapt the principle through their own PDCA cycles
Mandate an exact copy and audit compliance
Wait until both yards have the same equipment
Hire a consultant to write a company-wide standard
exam.why: When contexts differ, teaching the method and letting the receiving team adapt builds ownership and a better-fitting solution.
